'''Sherwood B. Idso''' (born June 12, 1942)<ref name=kirkham>{{cite book |title=Principles of Soil and Plant Water Relations |last=Kirkham |first=M.B. |year=2005 |publisher=[[Academic Press]] |isbn=978-0124097513 |page=451 |access-date=2012-08-18 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5r8AgAAQBAJ&pg=PA497}}</ref> was the president of the [[Center for the Study of Carbon Dioxide and Global Change]], which [[climate change denial|rejects the scientific consensus on climate change]]. Previously he was a Research Physicist with the [[U.S. Department of Agriculture]]'s [[Agricultural Research Service]] at the U.S. Water Conservation Laboratory in Phoenix, Arizona, where he worked since June 1967. He was also closely associated with [[Arizona State University]] over most of this period, serving as an adjunct professor in the Departments of Geology, Geography, and Botany and Microbiology. His two sons, [[Craig Idso|Craig]] and [[Keith Idso|Keith]], are, respectively, the founder<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.motherjones.com/environment/2009/12/dirty-dozen-climate-change-denial-11-idso-family%20%20 | title=No. 8: Center for the Study of Carbon Dioxide and Global Change (A.K.A. The Idso Family) | work=[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]] | date=4 December 2009 | access-date=15 March 2014 | author=Harkinson, Josh}}</ref> and vice president<ref>[https://www.co2science.org/about/vice_president.php Vice President], CO2Science</ref> of the Center for the Study of Carbon Dioxide and Global Change.

Idso was the author or co-author of over 500 publications including the books ''Carbon Dioxide: Friend or Foe?'' (1982) and ''Carbon Dioxide and Global Change: Earth in Transition'' (1989). He served on the editorial board of the international journal ''[[Agricultural and Forest Meteorology]]'' from 1973 to 1993 and since 1993 has served on the editorial board of ''[[Environmental and Experimental Botany]]''.  Over the course of his career, he has been an reviewer of manuscripts for 56 different scientific journals and 17 different funding agencies, representing an array of disciplines. He is an [[ISI highly cited researcher]].<ref name=ISI>{{cite web |url=http://highlycited.com/names/I.html |title=ISI Highly Cited: Sherwood B. Idso |publisher=[[Institute for Scientific Information]] |access-date=July 23, 2010}}</ref><ref name=isiarchive>{{cite web | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929111210/http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Browse&link2=Results&id=1340 | archive-date=September 29, 2007 | title=Idso, Sherwood B. | publisher=ISI HighlyCited.com| url=http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Browse&link2=Results&id=1340}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Sherwood Idso was born in [[Thief River Falls, Minnesota]] on June 12, 1942, where he lived until graduating from high school in 1960 as valedictorian.<ref name=kirkham/>  Idso also attended the [[University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering|Institute of Technology]] at the [[University of Minnesota]], receiving a B.Phys. in Physics with distinction in 1964, followed by an M.S. in Soil Science (with a minor in Physics) in 1966 and then a Ph.D. in Soil Science (with a minor in Meteorology and Mechanical Engineering) in 1968.<ref name=kirkham/><ref name=isiarchive/> His doctoral thesis was titled, ''The photosynthetic response of plants to their environment: a holocoenotic method of analysis''.<ref>{{cite journal | author=Idso, Sherwood B. | title=The photosynthetic response of plants to their environment: a holocoenotic method of analysis | publisher=[[University of Minnesota]] | year=1967| oclc=62428704 }}</ref>

==Climate science==
In 1972, Idso published an article called "An American [[Haboob]]", in which he documented a large dust storm in Arizona which occurred on July 16, 1971, and which stretched from [[Tucson]] to [[Phoenix, AZ|Phoenix]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Idso|first=S. B.|author2=Ingram, R. S. |author3=Pritchard, J. M. |title=An American Haboob|journal=Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society|date=October 1972|volume=53|issue=10|pages=930–935|doi=10.1175/1520-0477(1972)053<0930:AAH>2.0.CO;2|bibcode=1972BAMS...53..930I|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.azfamily.com/weather/An-American-Haboob--Part-3-121671484.html | title=An American Haboob Part 3 | work=[[Azfamily.com]] | date=11 May 2011 | access-date=17 April 2014 | author=Norman, Royal | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419014733/http://www.azfamily.com/weather/An-American-Haboob--Part-3-121671484.html | archive-date=19 April 2014 }}</ref>

In 1980, Idso published research which concluded that [[climate sensitivity]] was probably only about 0.3&nbsp;°C, about a tenth of the generally accepted value.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Idso|first=S. B.|title=The Climatological Significance of a Doubling of Earth's Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Concentration|journal=Science|date=28 March 1980|volume=207|issue=4438|pages=1462–1463|doi=10.1126/science.207.4438.1462|pmid=17779615|bibcode=1980Sci...207.1462I|s2cid=28241864 }}</ref> The following year, he opposed [[NASA]]'s global warming predictions, saying they were "about 10 times too great," adding that, in his view, global warming would have a beneficial effect on agriculture.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1981/1202/120228.html/(page)/2 | title=Is the world getting warmer? | work=[[Christian Science Monitor]] | date=2 December 1981 | access-date=25 March 2014 | author=Starr, Douglas}}</ref>

In 1984, Idso, along with A.J. Brazel, published a study in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' which concluded, contrary to a report the [[National Academy of Sciences]] released the previous year, that rising CO<sub>2</sub> levels would increase [[streamflow]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Idso|first=S. B.|author2=Brazel, A. J. |title=Rising atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations may increase streamflow|journal=Nature|date=1 November 1984|volume=312|issue=5989|pages=51–53|doi=10.1038/312051a0|url=https://naldc-legacy.nal.usda.gov/naldc/download.xhtml?id=50585&content=PDF|bibcode=1984Natur.312...51I|s2cid=4341851 |url-access=subscription}}{{dead link|date=June 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The study's authors argued that the NAS report came to the opposite conclusion because it neglected the effect of rising CO<sub>2</sub> levels on plants.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1984/1213/121323.html/(page)/2 | title=New CO[2] data undercuts dire prediction icecaps would melt. Chillier winters, hungrier bugs ahead? | work=Christian Science Monitor | date=13 December 1984 | access-date=27 March 2014 | author=Cowen, Robert C.}}</ref>

In the 1997 book, ''Global Warming: The Science and the Politics'' Idso said: "I find no compelling reason to believe that the earth will necessarily experience any global warming as a consequence of the ongoing rise in the atmosphere's carbon dioxide concentration."<ref>{{cite book | author=Jones, Laura | year=1997 | url=https://archive.org/details/globalwarmingsci0000unse | title=Global Warming: The Science and the Politics | publisher=[[Fraser Institute]] | isbn=978-0889751842 | url-access=registration }}</ref>

In the 1998 paper, ''{{CO2}}-induced global warming: a skeptic's view of potential climate change'' Idso said: "Several of these cooling forces have individually been estimated to be of equivalent magnitude, but of opposite sign, to the typically predicted [[greenhouse effect]] of a doubling of the air’s {{CO2}} content, which suggests to me that little net temperature change will ultimately result from the ongoing buildup of {{CO2}} in Earth's atmosphere."<ref>{{Cite journal | first1=Sherwood B. | last1=Idso | title={{CO2}}-induced global warming: a skeptic's view of potential climate change | journal=[[Climate Research (journal)|Climate Research]] | year=1998 | volume=10 | issue=1 | pages=69–82 | doi=10.3354/cr010069| bibcode=1998ClRes..10...69I | doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Personal life ==

=== Religion and Marriage ===
Idso was a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints. He was married and sealed to Carolyn Marie Wakefield in the Logan, Utah temple on August 23, 1963, whom he referred to as "the most beautiful woman in the world" in his diary. 

=== Family Life and Pastimes ===
Sherwood and Carolyn had seven children: his sons Grant, Keith, Craig, Lance, Wayne, and his daughters Jennifer and Julene. Idso was described as a very intelligent man, but also one who had a "great sense of humor." Idso held a lifelong fascination with nature as well as an enjoyment of photography, of which produced a variety of hobbies, such as capturing pictures of small creatures or assisting in the creation of a saltwater pond in the family home backyard.<ref>Funeral of {{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=98yB4CQwPEc |title=Sherwood Idso |language=en |access-date=2024-06-21 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Batesville® |title=Obituary for Sherwood Burtrum Idso at Tempe Mortuary |url=https://www.tempemortuary.com/obituary/sherwood-idso?lud=7DCEA42FFE3D5B5E40D58C06BAF9AC70 |access-date=2024-06-21 |website=www.tempemortuary.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Death ==
Idso died on June 12, 2024, on his 82nd birthday. He is interred in the Mesa City Cemetery in Mesa, AZ, and is survived by his wife, Carolyn.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards==
* 1977 - [[Arthur S. Flemming Award]] in recognition of "his innovative research into fundamental aspects of agricultural-climatological interrelationships affecting food production and the identification of achievable research goals whose attainment could significantly aid in assessment and improvement of world food supplies."<ref>{{cite web | url=http://flemming.gwu.edu/past-recipients-2/ | title=Arthur S. Fleming Award Recipients, 1948-2005 | publisher=[[George Washington University]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | author=Kirkham, M.B. | year=2005 | url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/book/9780124097513 | title=Principles of Soil and Plant Water Relations | publisher=[[Academic Press]]}}</ref>
* 2003 - [[Doctors for Disaster Preparedness#Petr Beckmann Award|Petr Beckmann Award]] for "courage and achievement in defense of scientific truth and freedom."<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.ddponline.org/ddpnews/ddpjul03.htm | title=Doctors for Disaster Preparedness Newsletter | date=July 2003 | publisher=[[Doctors for Disaster Preparedness]]}}</ref>
* 2014 - [[Frederick Seitz]] Memorial Award (presented by [[Heartland Institute]])
